jobs.title: Senior Director, Business Transformation, Trust Co.
jobs.description:
BMO Trust Company is a leading provider of trust, estate, fiduciary, and wealth administration services, supporting high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth individuals, families, and business owners across Canada. As part of BMO Private Wealth, BMO Trust works closely with Wealth Planning, Investment Management, Private Banking, and Trust & Estate professionals to deliver integrated solutions that help clients preserve, grow, and transfer wealth across generations.

The Senior Director, Business Transformation, Trust Co .,
leads the Trust Company's strategic growth, innovation, and transformation agenda. Responsible for identifying and executing initiatives that enhance client experience, drive business growth, and ensure the Trust Company remains aligned with evolving client needs, market opportunities, and Private Wealth priorities.

Fosters a culture aligned to BMO purpose, values and strategy and role models BMO values and behaviors in all that they do.
Ensures alignment between values and behavior that fosters diversity and inclusion.
Regularly connects work to BMO’s purpose, sets inspirational goals, defines clear expected outcomes, and ensures clear accountability for follow through.
Builds interdependent teams that collaborate across functional and operating groups to create the highest value for all stakeholders.
Attracts, retains, and enables the career development of top talent.
Improves team performance, recognizes and rewards performance, coaches employees, supports their development, and manages poor performance.
Monitors performance results at the national, market and sales-Trust professional level..
Identifies opportunities to grow business
Acts as a trusted advisor to senior leaders for making business decisions and implementing strategic initiatives.
Develops an expert understanding of business/group challenges.
Networks with industry contacts to gather competitive insights and best practices.
Recommends business priorities, advises on resource requirements and develops roadmap for strategic execution.
Manages resources and leads the execution of strategic initiatives to deliver on business, technology and financial goals.
Breaks down strategic problems, and analyses data and information to provide insights and recommendations.
Coordinates the management of databases; ensures alignment and integration of data in adherence with data governance standards.
Designs and produces regular and ad-hoc reports, financial reports and dashboards.
Leads change management programs of varying scope and type, including readiness assessments, planning, stakeholder management, execution, evaluation and sustainment of initiatives.
Leads the development and execution of the BMO Trust Company (internal and external) communications strategy, creating clear, impactful messaging that supports business objectives, strengthens employee and stakeholder engagement, and positively influences behaviors.
Leads / participates in the management of governance meetings including Board reporting and maintenance of governing body mandates, oversight and approval guidelines.
Leads/participates in the design, implementation and management of core business/group processes and technology investments
Oversees the provision of content and marketing materials for new business proposals e.g. special fee arrangements, technical information materials.
Operates at a group/enterprise-wide level and serves as a senior specialist resource across BMO.
Applies expertise and thinks creatively to address unique or ambiguous situations and to find solutions to multiple, interdependent, complex problems.
Fosters strong internal and external networks and works with and across multiple teams to achieve business objectives.
Take measured risks while protecting the bank by applying our Risk Management Framework in the execution of your role, in line with our Risk Culture and within our approved Risk Appetite while making sound and risk informed decisions that align to business strategy. protect assets, and adhere to applicable policy documents (Frameworks, Policies, Standards, Procedures and Supporting documents), laws and regulations.

Qualifications:

9+ years of relevant experience in related field is required.
Professional Certifications and/or Advanced Degrees preferred: TEP.
Completion of the CFA, MBA, CA or LLB is an asset
Expert knowledge and technical proficiency related to private wealth management strategies, issues and trends
Broad and diverse background in financial service industry and expert knowledge of the banking services for the high net worth (HNW) markets
Expert knowledge of all applicable compliance and industry regulations.
Seasoned expert with extensive industry knowledge.
Technical leader viewed as a thought leader for innovation.
Verbal & written communication skills - Expert.
Analytical and problem solving skills - Expert.
Influence skills - Expert.
Collaboration & team skills; with a focus on cross-group collaboration - Expert.
Able to manage ambiguity.
Data driven decision making - Expert.

$120,000.00 - $215,000.00

Salaried

jobs.title: DIRECTOR OF INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
jobs.description:
About The Lacroix Medical Group

A leader in private medicine in Quebec, the Lacroix Medical Group comprises three rapidly growing divisions:

Medical Clinics
Operating Rooms
Biomedical Laboratory

The organization has experienced strong and sustained growth since its founding in 2009 and currently employs nearly 350 people. As part of its strategic plan, the Group aims to accelerate its national and international development.

OUR MISSION

To be the benchmark in private healthcare.

OUR VALUES

Passion | Respect | Integrity | Commitment | Innovation.

The Mandate

In a context of sustained growth and transformation of its activities, Lacroix Medical Group is seeking a Director of Information Technology who will actively contribute to the organization's technological evolution.

Reporting directly to the President and CEO, the Director of IT plays a strategic role across the entire network. They are responsible for defining, structuring, and developing the IT function to effectively support the organization's operations, growth, and ambitions.

They provide leadership for technology strategy, infrastructure, business systems, cybersecurity, data governance, digital transformation, and artificial intelligence.

He is also responsible for the performance of his team and the organization's technology partner ecosystem. This role is for an experienced, business-oriented, and results-driven IT leader who can combine strategic vision with excellent execution. Your Key Responsibilities IT Strategy and Governance: Define and deploy the IT vision and master plan in line with the strategic, operational, and financial priorities of Groupe médical Lacroix. Advise senior management on investments, risks, and key technological choices.

Performance and Business Continuity

Ensure the performance, robustness, and high availability of the infrastructure and technology platforms essential to the network's medical and administrative activities, including ERP, CRM, DME, LIS, SaaS, and cloud environments.

Digital Transformation, Data, and Artificial Intelligence

Identify and prioritize initiatives to transform the organization through technology, data valorization, automation, and artificial intelligence. Lead major technology projects and ensure their effective integration into operations.

Cybersecurity and Risk Management

Maintain high standards in cybersecurity, information protection, redundancy, and business continuity in an environment where system availability and the protection of medical data are critical.

Leadership and Organizational Performance

Lead and develop a competent, autonomous, and accountable IT team. Establish clear objectives and performance indicators, ensure rigorous budget management, and optimize the contribution of suppliers, consultants, and technology partners.

An Executive Role Close to Operations

At Lacroix Medical Group, technology must meet the realities on the ground.

The IT Director will therefore need to maintain close contact with the various business units and network teams to understand their needs, anticipate challenges, and ensure that technological solutions contribute concretely to operational performance and service quality.

The position consequently requires excellent mobility. The successful candidate will be required to travel regularly throughout the Lacroix network in Quebec to meet with teams, support projects, and remain connected to the operational realities of the various facilities.

This on-the-ground presence is an essential component of the role and not an occasional responsibility.

The mandate expressly includes regular visits to service points.

The Ideal Candidate

We are looking for an experienced manager with a strong business acumen and excellent technological expertise, recognized for their leadership, judgment, and ability to drive organizational growth.

The Ideal Candidate Will Possess

A bachelor's degree in computer engineering, computer science, or a related field;
15 to 20 years of experience in information technology, including a minimum of 5 years in a management role;
Mastery of software architecture and project management;
A solid understanding of multi-site and cloud infrastructures;
Good knowledge of SaaS environments and major business platforms: ERP, CRM, financial systems, telephony, Microsoft 365, and others;
A thorough understanding of the issues cybersecurity, data governance and valorization, and artificial intelligence;
Proven experience in team management and development;
Recognized leadership in transformation and change management;
Ability to prioritize, make decisions, and manage effectively in a complex and evolving environment;
Excellent business acumen and the ability to communicate technological issues to senior management;
Fluency in French and English, both written and spoken;
A valid driver's license, a vehicle, and significant availability for regular travel throughout the network.

The Leader Profile We Are Looking For

Beyond technological expertise, we are looking for someone who stands out for their ability to mobilize, structure, and deliver.

A positive and committed leader with a strong sense of Accountability, the ability to build high-performing teams, manage rigorously, challenge the status quo, and transform technological challenges into concrete solutions for the business. The IT Director must be equally comfortable discussing strategy with senior management and understanding the challenges faced by teams in the field. Conditions and Compensation Lacroix Medical Group offers a competitive total compensation package including: Annual salary of $140,000 to $175,000, depending on experience and expertise; 4 weeks of vacation and 4 paid personal days; RRSP+ program with employer contribution; Cell phone allowance; Lacroix Health Credit; and an annual Lacroix gift card. This benefit can be combined with other benefits for personalized medical services.

Business travel expense account for trips outside your usual work area

Join a growing network and become a key player in the future of private medicine in Quebec.

Apply now and make a real difference.

jobs.title: Vice President Information Technology Services
jobs.description:
Our Client is seeking a transformative Information Technology Executive with a proven ability to lead high-performing teams, build innovation, modernization, and agility, with a drive for service, excellence and collaboration.

Our Client
is a not-for-profit healthcare insurance reciprocal that, together with its associated brokerage and corporate entities, provides comprehensive insurance, risk and claims management products and services to healthcare organizations across Canada. As a trusted healthcare safety advisor, Our Client is committed to delivering sustainable, responsive solutions that enhance safety across Canada's healthcare system.

As the largest not-for-profit healthcare liability insurer in Canada, Our Client serves more than 800 healthcare organizations (Subscribers) through the Reciprocal. Combining best-in-class insurance and claims management, sage counsel and risk management expertise, Our Client works collaboratively with its partners and Subscribers to advance safety across Canada's not-for-profit healthcare system.

Recognized as one of Greater Toronto's Top Employers for ten consecutive years, Our Client fosters a culture where employees are empowered to find innovative solutions, deliver exceptional service and make a meaningful difference.

Join Our Client and be part of a team committed to creating the safest healthcare system possible.

Vice President, Information Technology Services

Our Client has a record of over 99% Subscriber retention and has also benefited from substantive growth. With that in mind, Our Client is committed to continuing its strategic and exciting approach to innovation based on a grounding in data and digital capacity – all while focusing on data integrity, analysis, agility and responsive data governance and security. This focus on data, innovation, growth and excellence are key leadership priorities for the Vice President, Information Technology Services (VP). This role is integral to Our Client’s commitment to meeting the increasing and more diverse needs of its Subscribers and to maintain and enhance its best-in-class leadership capacity. This role will report directly to the Chief Executive Officer.

Our Client’s formal leaders are accountable, together with fellow leaders, for the overall accomplishment of Our Client’s strategic priorities including its Mission, Vision and Values and its Strategic Plan. As the leader of the Information Technology Service Department, the successful candidate will be instrumental in leading Our Client while holding primary responsibility for leading a high performing team consisting of infrastructure, applications, advanced analytics, and other information service professionals to build Our Client's capacity for innovation, modernization and agility while ensuring that these are achieved on a framework and structure that enhances security, protects the valuable and sensitive information that Our Client holds and which allows data to be used for the maximum of Our Client, its Subscribers and those they serve.

As a key member of Our Client's senior leadership team, the Vice President will provide strategic leadership across enterprise technology, digital transformation, data strategy and advanced analytics. The incumbent will oversee the modernization of technology infrastructure, applications and platforms, including cloud adoption and emerging technologies, while ensuring robust cybersecurity, data governance, regulatory compliance and enterprise risk management. Working collaboratively across Our Client's Group, the VP will align technology investments and initiatives with organizational priorities, enhance the experience of Subscribers/customers (internal and external), and serve as a trusted advisor to the CEO, senior leadership team and Board committees on technology strategy, innovation and risk.

Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate will have advanced people and leadership skills and aptitude, excellent communication skills and be a self-starter who enjoys working in a fast-paced environment. The ideal candidate will be comfortable operating in a mid-sized agile organization, is process-oriented, and experienced in supporting and initiating, with other leaders, a current culture focused on an unparalleled service orientation and a vision to the future that is transformation focused and which defines and embeds new beliefs and behaviours that will drive innovation. The combination of what works well and modernizing/sustaining structures and processes to enable resilience and support innovation in meeting customer needs, through advancing digital and analytics capabilities will ensure Our Client’s ability to leverage the power of information for improvement.

The successful candidate will bring a minimum of eight years of progressive senior leadership experience, with demonstrated expertise in enterprise technology strategy, financial and operational management, technology governance, cybersecurity and digital transformation. Experience leading complex modernization initiatives, including cloud adoption, data strategy, advanced analytics and legacy system transformation, will be important, as will a proven ability to build high-performing teams, oversee strategic technology investments, manage vendor relationships and deliver complex projects. The ideal candidate will possess strong business acumen, executive presence, sound judgement and exceptional communication skills, with experience advising Boards, senior leaders and diverse stakeholders. A bachelor's degree in information technology, business, engineering, healthcare or a related field is required, (a master's degree being preferred) and professional designations such as CISSP, CISA or PMP considered assets. Equivalent combinations of education and experience will be considered, and experience in healthcare or insurance is an asset. Above all, the successful candidate will be a collaborative, innovative leader with a passion and commitment to advancing a safer healthcare system for Canadians.

This position operates in a hybrid work environment, with regular business hours of Monday to Friday. Occasional evening meetings or events and travel within and between provinces may be required for Subscriber visits, presentations, conferences and professional development. A valid driver’s license and access to a vehicle are preferred.

We are committed to providing accommodations throughout the recruitment process. If you require accommodation, please notify us and we will work with you to meet your needs.

jobs.description:
At EY, we’re all in to shape your future with confidence.

We’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go.

Join EY and help to build a better working world.

The opportunity

As an Assistant Director, you will play a pivotal role in Canada’s EY wavespace and CX team, working with some of our most forward-thinking clients as they navigate complex business challenges and opportunities. You will work at the forefront of their transformation and AI agendas, helping to shape priorities and influence strategic direction.

Leveraging EY’s design thinking-based wavespace methodology, you will design and facilitate collaborative client sessions that foster alignment, generate innovative ideas, and enable informed strategic decision-making. You will play a key role in high-impact client projects and initiatives, bringing together diverse stakeholders to co-create solutions, shape innovation and transformation agendas, and deliver meaningful, actionable outcomes.

Through the global EY wavespace network, you will tap into leading practices, insights, and capabilities to deliver exceptional and differentiated client experiences. Learn more about EY wavespace here: EY wavespace

In addition, as part of our overarching CX strategy that includes a client listening program, you will have the opportunity to engage directly with senior executives, transforming their feedback into actionable insights that strengthen relationships and drive continuous improvement across client experiences.

This job posting relates to an existing vacancy within our organization.

Your Key Responsibilities

Lead end-to-end EY wavespace experiences, including:

Driving discovery phases to ensure an in depth understanding of clients’ current situation and future vision through interviews and/or review of strategic plans
Designing, preparing and executing immersive innovation sessions where you will:
Partner with clients to co-design the approach for the session
Identify and bring forward internal and/or external thought leaders, case studies and examples to inspire new perspectives
Synthesize and bring forward relevant insights from client discovery phase
Facilitate design-thinking based ideation and prioritization sessions to draw out innovative, value-generating opportunities
Build alignment across stakeholders to develop clear, actionable strategic roadmaps and plans
Leverage your creative ingenuity and our digital collaboration technologies to create exceptional and unique immersive experiences with our clients

Collaborating with EY account teams to debrief insights from EY wavespace engagements and client experience activities, helping to identify opportunities for continued value creation

Support and advance our client experience approach, including:

Meeting with clients from across industries to capture and synthesize their feedback on their experiences with EY
Assist in transforming perspectives into actionable insights and recommendations that strengthen relationships, enhance future engagements, and support opportunity development

Skills And Attributes For Success

Strong executive presence, with the confidence to engage and present at all levels
Excellent communication skills (oral and written), with the ability to deliver clear, concise, and impactful messages
Proven ability to build trusted relationships and collaborate effectively across teams and stakeholders
Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver high-quality outcomes
Demonstrated critical thinking and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate complex challenges into practical, actionable solutions
High emotional intelligence, cultural awareness, and ability to quickly establish credibility with clients and teams
Curiosity and adaptability, with comfort in navigating ambiguity and continuously learning
Strong understanding of digital trends and disruptions shaping client business landscapes
Commitment to delivering exceptional client experiences and coaching high-performing teams

To qualify for the role, you should have:

5-7 years of management consulting or equivalent business transformation or corporate strategy experience
Demonstrated project management skills
Expertise in design thinking tools and methods
This role involves interaction with clients operating nationally and globally where fluency in French and English is required. Bilingualism in both French and English is therefore a requirement of this role

Ideally, you’ll also have

Interest and comfort in leveraging AI tools to support ideation, research and session delivery
MBA or equivalent Master’s degree

What We Offer You

We offer a competitive compensation package where you’ll be rewarded based on your performance and recognized for the value you bring to our business. In addition, our Total Rewards package allows you decide which benefits are right for you and which ones help you create a solid foundation for your future. Our Total Rewards package includes a discretionary bonus program, a comprehensive medical, prescription drug and dental coverage plan, a defined contribution pension plan, a great vacation policy plus firm paid days that allow you to enjoy longer long weekends throughout the year, statutory holidays and paid personal days (based on province of residence), and a range of exciting programs and benefits designed to support your physical, financial and social well-being. Plus, we offer:

Support and coaching from some of the most engaging colleagues in the industry
Learning opportunities to develop new skills and progress your career
The freedom and flexibility to handle your role in a way that’s right for you

Are you ready to shape your future with confidence? Apply today.

To help create the best experience during the recruitment process, please describe any accommodations you may need.

Inclusiveness at EY

Inclusiveness is at the heart of who we are and how we work. We’re committed to fostering an environment where differences are valued, policies and practices are equitable, and our people feel a sense of belonging. We embrace diversity and are committed to combating systemic racism, advancing gender equity and women in leadership, advocating for the 2SLGBTQIA+ community, promoting our neuroinclusion and accessibility initiatives, and are dedicated to amplifying the voices of Indigenous peoples (First Nations, Inuit, and Métis) nationally as we strive towards reconciliation. Because when people feel free to be their authentic selves at work, they bring their best and are empowered to build a better working world.

jobs.title: Vice President, Enterprise Services
jobs.location: St John’s, Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada
jobs.description:
WorkplaceNL
administers Newfoundland and Labrador’s mandatory, no-fault workplace injury compensation system, funded by employer assessments and investment returns. We promote safe workplaces and provide benefits and services to injured workers, helping improve quality of life across the province.

Overview

Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, the Vice President, Enterprise Services brings an organization-wide perspective to strategy, performance, technology, people and enterprise risk.
This position provides executive leadership and strategic direction for Enterprise Services and is integral to WorkplaceNL’s modernization agenda, working in partnership with those leading transformation initiatives to ensure improvements are effectively integrated into ongoing operations. This is a long term temporary position, anticipated to span several years while WorkplaceNL advances its transformation and modernization program.

As a member of the Executive Team, you will help set WorkplaceNL’s direction and align people, resources and investments behind shared priorities. Your mandate extends beyond leading your portfolio: you will work across organizational boundaries, navigate competing needs and build support for changes that strengthen services and organizational performance.

You will also lead the continued development of WorkplaceNL’s Enterprise Risk Management Framework and report to the Board’s Governance Committee.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

Strategy and planning:
Working with the Executive Team and senior leaders to translate long-term priorities into evidence-based, multi-year plans with clear accountabilities and measurable outcomes.

Technology and information management:
Guiding technology investments, budgets and service delivery to support organizational priorities. Overseeing information management, cybersecurity and business resilience, and advising senior leaders and the Board on technology opportunities and risks.

Performance and improvement:
Leading corporate performance measurement, reporting and continuous improvement. Overseeing Internal Review, program evaluation and quality assurance, and guiding compliance with the Transparency and Accountability Act, annual performance reporting and CEO performance contracts.

Policy and government relations:
Guiding the policy framework and annual policy plan, overseeing statutory reviews and legislative priorities, and maintaining productive relationships with government and other stakeholders.

People and culture:
Setting the context for HR strategies that support employee health and safety, engagement, recruitment, retention and succession. Working with leaders to strengthen organizational capability and foster an ethical, inclusive and accountable workplace.

Enterprise risk:
Strengthening risk management across the organization, ensuring risks inform planning, investment and operational decisions, with clear reporting to the Executive Team and Board.

Who you are

You lead with an enterprise perspective, making decisions based on what serves the organization as a whole. You build trust across functions and understand the people dynamics that shape organizational performance. You can surface competing interests, work through disagreement and bring people together around a clear direction. Where delivery relies on shared resources, you help leaders make sound trade-offs, establish priorities and agree on how work will move forward.
You are comfortable leading change and transformation through influence, ingenuity as well as authority. You communicate the reasons for change clearly, build commitment and maintain accountability for results. You develop strong leaders, address concerns directly and create the conditions for teams to work effectively together.

You bring sound judgement and executive presence to discussions with the CEO, Board, government, and other stakeholders. You can explain complex issues clearly, offer candid advice and connect operational decisions to strategy, risk, financial stewardship and client service.

What you bring:

A university degree in business, public administration, humanities, science or relevant disciplines. A master’s degree in a relevant discipline would be considered an asset.
Minimum of ten years of progressive management experience in a public or private organization leading multiple lines of business and providing services to diverse client groups.
Demonstrated ability to navigate a public sector environment, balancing government priorities, board oversight, public accountability and organizational objectives.
Strong leadership abilities with exceptional interpersonal and communication skills and a proven track record of building effective stakeholder relationships.
Experience conceptualizing and executing strategies that advance cross-organizational priorities, including in the areas of information technology, data and analytics.
Experience applying best practices in enterprise risk management.
Experience with project planning, management and governance, especially as it relates to information technology.
Ability to think strategically, analytically, and use good judgement in providing oversight and solutions to corporate opportunities, challenges and risks.

Why Join Us?
Impactful work that contributes to the work safety in Newfoundland and Labrador.
Competitive base salary; range $126,040 - $163,852
Generous vacation and leave entitlements.
Comprehensive health and dental benefits.
Enrollment in the Public Service Pension Plan.
Opportunities for ongoing professional development.
A collaborative, supportive, and inclusive work environment.

Candidates of all backgrounds including but not limited to individuals with international experience, newcomers to Canada, women, Indigenous persons, persons with disabilities, members of visible minorities, and persons of various gender identities and sexual orientations are encouraged to apply. jobs.title: Director of Solution Architecture
jobs.description:
At PwC Canada, we're transforming the way we work—and the way our people and clients experience technology. Our Products & Technology team builds the digital products, enterprise applications, and AI-enabled platforms that power the firm and shape the future of professional services. We're a community of solvers combining technology, data, and human ingenuity to deliver sustained outcomes that matter. We're looking for a Director of Solution Architecture to lead our established team of Senior Solution Architects—a technically deep, business-savvy leader who can set direction, grow and develop talent, and partner with senior leaders across the firm to turn ambitious ideas into reality. Reporting to the Architecture and Development Leader, you will lead PwC Canada's Solution Architecture practice within Products & Technology. You will take ownership of our established team of Senior Solution Architects, elevate their performance, and grow the team's capabilities as our technology ambitions expand. The team designs AI-enabled products, enterprise applications, and platforms used across the firm's lines of service, ensuring our solutions are secure, scalable, resilient, aligned with enterprise architecture standards—and deliver real business value. This is a hands-on architecture leadership role. While your focus is on design and technical direction rather than execution, you'll be expected to understand the technology from the inside. You'll go deep into architecture diagrams, integration designs, data flows, platform configurations, and the realities of how solutions are implemented, engaging with technical trade-offs at a practitioner level. Your credibility with the team and with stakeholders will come from genuine technical depth and a willingness to go hands-on with architecture and implementation details when the situation calls for it, not from high-level concepts alone. Equally, this role operates at the intersection of business and technology. You'll be a trusted advisor to business stakeholders and organizational leaders, translating complex challenges into clear technology solutions, influencing strategic direction, and communicating in terms that resonate with executives. You'll also help shape how PwC Canada adopts emerging technologies, including generative and agentic AI.

The Opportunity

As a Director of Solution Architecture, unlock your potential and embrace the chance to drive meaningful outcomes that’ll elevate your career. Your role will include, but isn’t limited to:

Provide architecture oversight for digital products, enterprise applications, and AI-enabled solutions from ideation through production
Lead solution design decisions, balancing reusable platform components with business-specific needs
Guide the architecture of enterprise applications—including SaaS platforms, ERP, CRM, HR, finance, and collaboration systems—ensuring effective integration, extensibility, and alignment with our broader technology ecosystem
Go hands-on with architecture and technical implementation details when needed—working through complex integration patterns, data flows, platform configurations, or design problems alongside the team
Advise on the adoption of emerging technologies, including generative and agentic AI
Manage, coach, and mentor an established team of talented Senior Solution Architects, elevating performance and fostering a culture of technical excellence and continuous learning
Grow the team's capabilities over time—identifying skill gaps, developing talent from within, and recruiting new members as the practice expands
Evolve team structure and define new roles as the practice grows and technology priorities shift
Partner with Enterprise Architecture, Data, Security, and Risk teams to ensure solutions align with firm standards
Participate in architecture review boards and technology governance forums, advising on governance requirements, risk assessments, and policy exceptions
Contribute to PwC's broader architecture community—locally and across the global PwC network

What You’ll Bring

Your skills, knowledge, and experiences are what set you apart. Here’s what we look for:

Experience in technology roles, including significant time in solution or enterprise architecture, with extensive experience designing and delivering solutions within large, complex organizations
Proven experience leading, developing, and growing a team of Senior Solution Architects—setting technical direction, elevating performance, and fostering a high-performance culture, including in an Agile/DevOps environment
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science or Computer Engineering
Azure Cloud Platform certifications (Solutions Architect or Developer) preferred; TOGAF certification

jobs.title: Interim Chief Information Officer
jobs.description:
IMMEDIATE INTERIM OPPORTUNITY

Interim Chief Information Officer

Reports to: President

Location: Greater Toronto Area, Ontario

Duration: 6-12 Months

Hybrid working

Our client, a large and complex Ontario post-secondary institution, is seeking an accomplished Interim Chief Information Officer
to provide leadership through an important period of transition, modernization and organizational evolution.

This is an exciting opportunity for a seasoned technology executive who can combine strategic thinking with hands-on execution
.

The organization recognizes that technology has the potential to play a much greater role in how it operates, how decisions are made, how services are delivered and how students experience the institution. The Interim CIO will be asked not simply to manage the existing technology environment, but to challenge conventional thinking about how technology is deployed and where it can fundamentally improve the operating model.

Leading a team of more than 100 technology professionals, the successful executive will initially provide stability, clarity and leadership through transition. Beyond this, they will help establish the priorities, capabilities, operating model and roadmap required for the next stage of the organization's technology journey.

This is therefore a mandate for a builder, modernizer and objective disruptor
, someone able to respect what is working while constructively challenging what could be done differently.

The Mandate

The Interim CIO will provide overall leadership to the technology function while working closely with the organization's senior leadership team to determine how technology can better enable its academic, student and operational priorities.

A central component of the mandate will be assessing the technology operating model
and identifying opportunities to improve effectiveness, service, scalability and value.
The Interim CIO will be expected to create alignment between technology strategy and organizational strategy, while maintaining a bias toward execution and measurable outcomes.

Key priorities will include:

Technology Strategy & Operating Model

Assess the current technology environment, capabilities, organizational structure and priorities and establish a clear roadmap for the next phase of modernization.
Challenge existing assumptions around how technology services are organized, delivered and supported.
Identify opportunities to simplify processes, reduce complexity, improve scalability and improve the value generated from technology investment
.
Evaluate the appropriate balance between internal capabilities, external partnerships, managed services and selective outsourcing.
Introduce stronger prioritization and governance disciplines to ensure technology resources are focused on the areas of greatest institutional impact.
Translate technology strategy into a practical execution agenda with clear accountabilities and outcomes.

Leadership Through Change

The Interim CIO will inherit a substantial team of 100+ technology professionals
and will need to quickly establish credibility and provide visible, confident leadership.

The organization operates within a unionized environment. Accordingly, the executive must understand how to lead meaningful organizational and operational change while respecting collective agreements, established processes and employee relationships.

The successful individual will:

Provide stability and clarity during transition.
Assess organizational capability, structure and accountabilities.
Coach and develop technology leaders.
Build stronger accountability for results.
Engage employees in the modernization journey.
Create a strong service and performance culture.
Navigate change thoughtfully within a complex unionized environment
.
Maintain momentum while making difficult decisions where required.

ERP Optimization & Enterprise Platforms

An important priority will be continuing to optimize the organization's ERP and broader enterprise technology environment.

The Interim CIO will:

Assess the current ERP implementation and identify opportunities to increase adoption, functionality and organizational value.
Address process, integration, data and operating-model issues that may inhibit the organization from realizing the full value of its enterprise platforms.
Challenge the proliferation of unnecessary processes, applications and workarounds where these create complexity.
Ensure technology modernization is accompanied by process modernization rather than simply automating existing ways of working
.
Strengthen the connection between enterprise systems, organizational processes and user experience.

Cybersecurity, Risk & Resilience

Cybersecurity will be a significant part of the mandate.

The Interim CIO will assess and evolve the organization's cybersecurity posture, governance and protocols, ensuring they remain appropriate for a large, complex and highly distributed post-secondary environment.

The executive will work to strengthen areas including security governance, accountability, organizational awareness and operational resilience, while ensuring cybersecurity is understood as an enterprise risk rather than simply an IT responsibility
.

The successful candidate will balance increasingly sophisticated security requirements with the accessibility, flexibility and innovation expected within a modern educational institution.

Cloud & Technology Modernization

The organization has begun elements of its cloud journey, but further opportunity remains to modernize its technology architecture and operating environment.

The Interim CIO will assess where further migration and modernization create genuine operational, financial, resilience or user-experience benefits.

They will bring an objective perspective regarding cloud strategy, legacy environments, technical debt, architecture and application rationalization
, ensuring modernization is driven by institutional value rather than technology for technology's sake.

Data Governance, Analytics & Decision Support

Data represents a significant opportunity for the organization.

The Interim CIO will help establish stronger data governance, ownership, quality and analytics capabilities
, enabling leaders across the institution to make better and faster decisions based on reliable information.

The mandate will include helping the organization move beyond reporting toward a culture where trusted data and actionable insights routinely inform operational, financial, academic and student-focused decision-making.

This will require both technology leadership and the ability to address the governance, accountability and behavioural changes necessary to establish a more mature data culture.

Artificial Intelligence

The organization recognizes the potentially significant role AI could play in both its operating model and the broader evolution of post-secondary education.

The Interim CIO will help leadership distinguish between experimentation and sustainable enterprise adoption, identifying practical opportunities where AI, automation and emerging technologies can improve productivity, decision-making and service delivery
.

Equally important will be establishing appropriate governance around the adoption of these technologies, including cybersecurity, privacy, data, risk and responsible use.

The successful executive will bring curiosity and ambition around AI while maintaining the pragmatic judgment required to translate emerging technology into sustainable institutional value.

The Evolving Student Experience

Technology is increasingly integral to the complete student journey.

How students learn, interact with faculty, access services, consume information and engage with an institution continues to evolve.

The Interim CIO will work across the organization to consider how technology can help create a simpler, more integrated, personalized and contemporary student experience
.

The opportunity extends beyond classroom technology. It is about understanding how technology can differentiate the institution and reduce friction across the entire student journey.

Service Culture

A key leadership priority will be continuing to evolve the technology function toward a highly responsive, accountable and customer-focused service organization.

The Interim CIO will establish clear expectations around service delivery, ownership, responsiveness and partnership with internal stakeholders.

Technology should increasingly be viewed as an enabler and partner to the organization
, rather than simply a provider of systems and infrastructure.

The Ideal Interim Executive

The successful candidate will be an accomplished CIO or senior enterprise technology executive
who has led a sizeable, complex technology function through significant modernization and organizational change.

They will bring experience across a combination of:

Enterprise technology strategy and execution.
Leadership of large, multidisciplinary technology teams.
Technology operating-model transformation.
ERP and enterprise application optimization.
Cloud migration and modernization.
Cybersecurity, risk and technology governance.
Data governance, analytics and information management.
AI, automation and emerging technologies.
Process optimization and organizational simplification.
Managed services, strategic sourcing and outsourcing.
Vendor and commercial management.
Digital/customer experience transformation.
Leadership in a unionized environment.
Organizational change and talent development.

Experience within higher education or the broader public sector
would be highly relevant, although the organization will also be interested in executives from other large, complex and regulated environments who can bring fresh thinking and transferable experience.

Leadership Style

This mandate requires more than technical credibility.

The ideal executive will be pragmatic, curious, commercially minded and comfortable challenging the status quo
. They will know when to listen and preserve institutional knowledge, but equally when to push the organization toward a different approach.

They will be capable of moving comfortably between the boardroom and the technology organization, translating complex technology issues into clear discussions about risk, cost, service, productivity and organizational outcomes
.

Most importantly, this individual will be an objective disruptor with strong execution discipline
.
They will leave the organization not simply with better technology, but with a stronger technology function, clearer priorities, improved governance, better use of data, enhanced cybersecurity and a pragmatic roadmap for how technology can enable the institution's future operating model.

The attraction of the assignment

For an experienced CIO, this is a rare opportunity to have meaningful impact in a relatively short period.

The mandate combines people leadership, technology modernization, ERP optimization, cyber, cloud, data and analytics, AI, operating-model transformation and student experience
within one of the most rapidly changing sectors in Canada.

The successful interim will have the platform to challenge existing thinking, accelerate decisions and help redefine the role technology plays across the institution.

This is not a mandate to simply keep the lights on. It is an opportunity to shape what technology leadership, capability and service should look like for the organization's next chapter.

Develop and implement information management strategies and polices to ensure the secure and efficient handling of Court information.
Project management, change management and strategic planning processes for the effective delivery and management of both short and long-term information technology goals set by the judiciary.
Represent the interests of the judiciary recognizing judicial independence in their day-today operations of and/or projects involving implementing and/or updating software, databases and digital tools used by the judiciary or involving judicial data and court information.
Must operate with full confidence of the Chief Justices and the Chief Judge, be discreet as required and understand the highly confidential and sensitive nature of the work that they perform.
The Chief Court Information Officer (“CCIO”) must have the ability to work cooperatively and harmoniously with all members of the judiciary and both senior and front-line court administration staff, as we as internal and external stakeholders.
Lead the modernization of court information systems, including case management, e-filing, digital evidence, and courtroom technology.

Qualifications

Education and/or training involving computer science, information technology, cyber security or related field.

Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively with stakeholders at all levels of the organization.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to develop and implement effective information management strategies for an increasingly digital legal work environment.
Extensive experience conducting IT and information security research and providing advice and opinions, preferably at a senior executive level.
Demonstrated ability to prepare written opinions, memoranda and reports.

Experience using MS Office, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Visio and Outlook and online legal research databases which may be used by the judiciary. Familiarity with JUDICLOUD (federally appointed judges email network) and/or PowerBI is considered an asset.

Must be able to provide a satisfactory criminal record check and security clearance.

Relevant certifications such as the Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP)
A law degree from an accredited university or college recognized in Manitoba.

Present clear financial results and business insights to senior leadership

Process Improvement & Governance

Drive continuous improvement in FP&A processes, planning models, and reporting frameworks.
Ensure alignment with corporate finance requirements, accounting policies, and internal controls
Support month-end close and planning processes in partnership with accounting and finance teams.

Qualifications

CPA, CMA, CFA, or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.
Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business strongly preferred.
Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and business analysis skills.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and experience with ERP and planning/reporting systems.
Executive presence with strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and regions.

Preferred Experience In a Service Business

Experience analyzing operational KPIs such as technician utilization, service efficiency, contract margins, backlog, renewal rates, and service attach rates.

Core Competencies

Strategic leadership
Financial and commercial acumen
Analytical rigor
Executive business partnership

Problem solving
Process improvement
Results orientation and a bias for action

Team Development

new_jobs.title: Vice President, Enterprise Services
new_jobs.location: St John’s, Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada
new_jobs.description:
WorkplaceNL
administers Newfoundland and Labrador’s mandatory, no-fault workplace injury compensation system, funded by employer assessments and investment returns. We promote safe workplaces and provide benefits and services to injured workers, helping improve quality of life across the province.

Overview

Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, the Vice President, Enterprise Services brings an organization-wide perspective to strategy, performance, technology, people and enterprise risk.
This position provides executive leadership and strategic direction for Enterprise Services and is integral to WorkplaceNL’s modernization agenda, working in partnership with those leading transformation initiatives to ensure improvements are effectively integrated into ongoing operations. This is a long term temporary position, anticipated to span several years while WorkplaceNL advances its transformation and modernization program.

As a member of the Executive Team, you will help set WorkplaceNL’s direction and align people, resources and investments behind shared priorities. Your mandate extends beyond leading your portfolio: you will work across organizational boundaries, navigate competing needs and build support for changes that strengthen services and organizational performance.

You will also lead the continued development of WorkplaceNL’s Enterprise Risk Management Framework and report to the Board’s Governance Committee.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

Strategy and planning:
Working with the Executive Team and senior leaders to translate long-term priorities into evidence-based, multi-year plans with clear accountabilities and measurable outcomes.

Technology and information management:
Guiding technology investments, budgets and service delivery to support organizational priorities. Overseeing information management, cybersecurity and business resilience, and advising senior leaders and the Board on technology opportunities and risks.

Performance and improvement:
Leading corporate performance measurement, reporting and continuous improvement. Overseeing Internal Review, program evaluation and quality assurance, and guiding compliance with the Transparency and Accountability Act, annual performance reporting and CEO performance contracts.

Policy and government relations:
Guiding the policy framework and annual policy plan, overseeing statutory reviews and legislative priorities, and maintaining productive relationships with government and other stakeholders.

People and culture:
Setting the context for HR strategies that support employee health and safety, engagement, recruitment, retention and succession. Working with leaders to strengthen organizational capability and foster an ethical, inclusive and accountable workplace.

Enterprise risk:
Strengthening risk management across the organization, ensuring risks inform planning, investment and operational decisions, with clear reporting to the Executive Team and Board.

Who you are

You lead with an enterprise perspective, making decisions based on what serves the organization as a whole. You build trust across functions and understand the people dynamics that shape organizational performance. You can surface competing interests, work through disagreement and bring people together around a clear direction. Where delivery relies on shared resources, you help leaders make sound trade-offs, establish priorities and agree on how work will move forward.
You are comfortable leading change and transformation through influence, ingenuity as well as authority. You communicate the reasons for change clearly, build commitment and maintain accountability for results. You develop strong leaders, address concerns directly and create the conditions for teams to work effectively together.

You bring sound judgement and executive presence to discussions with the CEO, Board, government, and other stakeholders. You can explain complex issues clearly, offer candid advice and connect operational decisions to strategy, risk, financial stewardship and client service.

What you bring:

A university degree in business, public administration, humanities, science or relevant disciplines. A master’s degree in a relevant discipline would be considered an asset.
Minimum of ten years of progressive management experience in a public or private organization leading multiple lines of business and providing services to diverse client groups.
Demonstrated ability to navigate a public sector environment, balancing government priorities, board oversight, public accountability and organizational objectives.
Strong leadership abilities with exceptional interpersonal and communication skills and a proven track record of building effective stakeholder relationships.
Experience conceptualizing and executing strategies that advance cross-organizational priorities, including in the areas of information technology, data and analytics.
Experience applying best practices in enterprise risk management.
Experience with project planning, management and governance, especially as it relates to information technology.
Ability to think strategically, analytically, and use good judgement in providing oversight and solutions to corporate opportunities, challenges and risks.

Why Join Us?
Impactful work that contributes to the work safety in Newfoundland and Labrador.
Competitive base salary; range $126,040 - $163,852
Generous vacation and leave entitlements.
Comprehensive health and dental benefits.
Enrollment in the Public Service Pension Plan.
Opportunities for ongoing professional development.

Job Description

On behalf of our public-sector client, Affinity is seeking a Chief Courts Information Officer to be accountable for the strategic leadership, governance, and delivery of information management (IM), information technology (IT), and digital services for the Courts. The CCIO ensures that court information systems, digital services, and technology investments support judicial independence, court administration, access to justice, operational efficiency, privacy, and security.

Responsibilities

Develop and implement information management strategies and polices to ensure the secure and efficient handling of Court information.
Project management, change management and strategic planning processes for the effective delivery and management of both short and long-term information technology goals set by the judiciary.
Represent the interests of the judiciary recognizing judicial independence in their day-today operations of and/or projects involving implementing and/or updating software, databases and digital tools used by the judiciary or involving judicial data and court information.
Must operate with full confidence of the Chief Justices and the Chief Judge, be discreet as required and understand the highly confidential and sensitive nature of the work that they perform.
The Chief Court Information Officer (“CCIO”) must have the ability to work cooperatively and harmoniously with all members of the judiciary and both senior and front-line court administration staff, as we as internal and external stakeholders.
Lead the modernization of court information systems, including case management, e-filing, digital evidence, and courtroom technology.

Qualifications

Education and/or training involving computer science, information technology, cyber security or related field.
Significant work experience, preferably 5 years or more, in information technology and information governance, with a focus on cybersecurity and records retention.
Strong understanding of legal and regulatory requirements related to information management, cybersecurity, and records retention.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively with stakeholders at all levels of the organization.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to develop and implement effective information management strategies for an increasingly digital legal work environment.
Extensive experience conducting IT and information security research and providing advice and opinions, preferably at a senior executive level.
Demonstrated ability to prepare written opinions, memoranda and reports.
The incumbent must have a superior understanding of the principles of judicial independence and possess strong political acumen and experience in the application of discretion and diplomacy to ensure positive outcomes and confidence in the administration of justice.
Well-developed planning and organizational skills in order to accomplish the position’s responsibilities and meet target dates and set priorities.
Experience using MS Office, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Visio and Outlook and online legal research databases which may be used by the judiciary. Familiarity with JUDICLOUD (federally appointed judges email network) and/or PowerBI is considered an asset.
Stakeholder engagement - Build effective relationships with the judiciary, court administrators, justice partners, central government IT organizations, and external stakeholders.
Represent the Courts on inter jurisdictional, justice sector, and government technology forums, as required.
Communicate complex technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences.
On-site attendance is a mandatory requirement for this role.
Must be able to provide a satisfactory criminal record check and security clearance.
The Resource will be required to execute a Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) and maintain strict confidentiality with respect to all information obtained or accessed in the course of performing the Services.
Relevant certifications such as the Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP)
A law degree from an accredited university or college recognized in Manitoba.
